sets.s: Having a healthy breakfast is essential in providing you with the energy you need to start your day.
i: Breakfast is the most important meal of the day.
N
The statement states that breakfast is essential, but it does not compare it to other meals so we cannot assume it is more important than others.
It's good to eat a healthy breakfast.
M
The statement is implying that a healthy breakfast is good.
It’s harder to efficiently get started with your day without a healthy breakfast.
M

The statement says that having a healthy breakfast is ‘essential’ in providing you the energy you need to start your day. Therefore, it is logically justified to state that you cannot efficiently get started without a healthy breakfast.

sets.s: Matt, don’t you know that listening to rhythmic music whilst studying can negatively affect your ability to retain information? Do not listen to any music, and work in silence for best retention of information.
i: Listening to rhythmic music whilst working could hinder ability to work effectively.
M
The statement only talks about retaining information, and that listening to rhythmic music hinders that ability which is assumed in the passage. Therefore, assumption made.
Matt was listening to rhythmic music whilst studying.
M
It is a fair assumption that Matt’s friend said this because Matt was listening to rhythmic music whilst studying.
Matt did not previously know this information.
N
The statement is just someone telling Matt this information as if he didn’t already know it, even though he might have known it.

sets.s: Owners of a limited company end up paying less National Insurance Contributions (NICs) than sole traders with similarly sized businesses structured in exactly the same way.
i: Sole traders pay more tax than owners of limited companies.
N
The statement claims that sole traders pay more NICs, so the statement is not comparing the two types of company’s overall tax.
Paying less NIC tax is an advantage when creating a limited company over becoming a sole trader.
M

The statement is states that a limited company pays less in NICs, but it does not compare the advantages of this. Given it at minimum in isolation, it is certainly an advantage to pay less NIC as a limited company than a sole trader.
Sole traders in general pay higher NICs than limited companies.
M
The statement relies on the fact that it is comparing two fairly identical businesses, so the average costs of tax would be lower for a limited company.

sets.s: The director promised that he wasn’t going to impose a reorganisation of the company before he was elected, but he failed to keep this promise when he reorganised it anyway.
i: The shareholders did not want a reorganisation of the company.
N
The director made this promise, but we have no indication of what the shareholders want. Therefore, it is assumption not made.
The director should stick to their promise.
N
The statement is only saying that the director didn’t adhere to his promise, not that it was the right or wrong thing to do.
The promise may have helped towards getting him to become elected.
M

The statement implies that he did not stick to the promise that he made before he was elected and it is implied that the employees wanted him to not reorganise it, so it is safe to assume he made this promise to help increase his chances of being elected.
